locations.name: Border / Port of Entry
locations.description: The line between before and after. Chain-link and fluorescent light. Someone's playing a radio in Spanish three cars back.
ambient_details: A fly lands on the booth window. It has been here longer than you.
The air conditioning unit drips onto the concrete in a rhythm that could be morse code but isn't.
Someone left a half-eaten breakfast burrito on the checkpoint barrier. No one will claim it.
The flag hangs perfectly still. There is no wind here. There is never wind here.
A dog sniffs luggage with the enthusiasm of someone who loves their job and hates Mondays.
The fluorescent lights hum in B-flat. You are not the first person to notice this.
A child in the next lane waves at you through a car window. You are not sure if waving back is legal.
The parking lot has three types of vehicles: government, desperate, and rental.
A sign says WELCOME in four languages. The font gets smaller with each translation.
The ceiling tiles have water stains that look like countries that don't exist anymore.

events.title: The Primary Inspection
events.description: A booth agent waves you forward. The line behind you exhales.
events.narrator_line: The booth smells like hand sanitizer and decisions.

events.title: Secondary Screening
events.description: A second agent appears. They want to talk about your luggage.
events.narrator_line: Secondary screening is where stories go to be tested against themselves.

events.title: The Helpful Coyote
events.description: Someone in the parking lot knows a way across. For a price.
events.narrator_line: Generosity with a price tag is just commerce wearing a smile.

events.title: The Shelter Volunteer
events.description: A woman with a clipboard and tired eyes offers water and a phone charger.
events.narrator_line: She has heard every story. Yours is not special. She will help anyway.

events.title: The Other Side of the Line
events.description: Someone ahead of you gets turned back. They walk past you without looking up.
events.narrator_line: Deportation is a word that sounds like a door closing. Because it is.

events.title: The Night Shift Agent
events.description: The shift change brings someone new. They haven't had coffee yet.
events.narrator_line: The night shift exists in a timezone that is neither today nor yesterday.

events.title: The Bail Bondsman's Card
events.description: A man in a polo shirt hands you a business card. 'Just in case,' he says.
events.narrator_line: His smile is the only thing in this parking lot that has been professionally whitened.

events.title: The Notary Public
events.description: A strip mall notary offers to certify your documents. Her office smells like toner and regret.
events.narrator_line: A notary stamp does not make something true. It makes something official. These are different things.

events.title: The Truck Stop Waitress
events.description: She refills your coffee without asking and calls you 'hon.' The check comes with a warning.
events.narrator_line: Truck stop waitresses know more about border policy than most senators. They just don't get a vote.

events.title: The Ranch Hand
events.description: He saw you from the fence line. He's deciding whether to care.
events.narrator_line: In ranch country, minding your own business is both a philosophy and a land-use policy.

events.title: The Gas Station Encounter
events.description: The cashier looks at your ID longer than necessary. The security camera blinks red.
events.narrator_line: Gas stations near the border sell three things: fuel, snacks, and the feeling of being watched.

events.title: The Church Basement
events.description: A pastor opens the church at night. No questions. Rice and beans. A mat on the floor.
events.narrator_line: The kingdom of heaven has a strict no-questions policy, apparently.

events.title: The Off-Duty Deputy
events.description: He's getting coffee. He's not on duty. He notices you anyway.
events.narrator_line: Off-duty law enforcement is a legal concept, not a behavioral one.

events.title: The Motel Night Manager
events.description: Cash only. No names. The ice machine doesn't work. He seems fine with all of this.
events.narrator_line: The motel has two stars on Google. Both reviewers mentioned the parking.

events.title: The Pharmacy Tech
events.description: She asks if you have insurance. The answer is obvious. She gives you a look that costs nothing.
events.narrator_line: The pharmacy is next to the border like a bandage next to the thing that cuts you.

events.title: Checkpoint Charlie
events.description: An interior checkpoint 50 miles from the border. They're checking everyone.
events.narrator_line: The Constitution applies differently at different distances from the border. This is called 'the reasonable suspicion gradient.'

events.title: Wrong Bus
events.description: You got on the bus to El Centro. El Centro is not where you're going.
events.narrator_line: Geography is the original skill check.

events.title: Document Discrepancy
events.description: The date on one paper doesn't match the date on another. You know this. They don't. Yet.
events.narrator_line: Bureaucracy is a machine that runs on consistency. You have just introduced an inconsistency.

events.title: Phone Battery Dies
events.description: Your phone dies. Your contact's number was on your phone.
events.narrator_line: The modern era's version of losing the treasure map.

events.title: The Flat Tire
events.description: The ride you arranged has a flat. The driver looks at you like this is your fault.
events.narrator_line: Correlation is not causation. But try telling that to a man with a lug wrench.

events.title: Heat Advisory
events.description: 115 degrees. The road shimmers. Your water is warm.
events.narrator_line: The desert does not have an opinion about your immigration status.

events.title: Someone Recognizes You
events.description: A face from three days ago appears. They're talking to an agent.
events.narrator_line: In a system built on anonymity, being remembered is a crisis.

events.title: Rain on the Rio Grande
events.description: The river crossing you planned is now the river crossing nobody should plan.
events.narrator_line: Nature does not file for permits.

events.title: The Locked Gate
events.description: The route you were told about leads to a locked gate with a camera.
events.narrator_line: The difference between a gate and a wall is mostly philosophical until you need to get through one.

events.title: No Room at the Shelter
events.description: Full. The list is three days long. A cot appears to be made of hope and federal funding.
events.narrator_line: Capacity is measured in bodies. Dignity is not measured.

events.title: The Unguarded Moment
events.description: The shift change creates a ten-minute window. Someone mentions this casually.
events.narrator_line: Ten minutes is either a coffee break or a life decision. Context matters.

events.title: The Sympathetic Agent
events.description: One agent processes people faster than the others. The line adjusts.
events.narrator_line: Compassion in bureaucracy looks like speed.

events.title: Lost and Found
events.description: Someone left a bag at the checkpoint. Inside: a bus ticket, a phone charger, $20.
events.narrator_line: Finders keepers is not recognized by international law. Neither is losers weepers.

events.title: The Work Offer
events.description: A ranch needs hands for two days. Cash. No questions.
events.narrator_line: Manual labor is the universal language.

events.title: The Phone Call
events.description: A stranger offers you their phone. One call. Make it count.
events.narrator_line: Generosity from strangers is either grace or a setup. You cannot tell which until after.

events.title: The Information Trade
events.description: Someone knows which agents are working tomorrow. This information has a price.
events.narrator_line: Intelligence is just gossip with consequences.

events.title: The Ride Offer
events.description: A trucker heading north has room. The cab smells like pine air freshener and long decisions.
events.narrator_line: Every ride is a contract. The terms are negotiated in eye contact.

events.title: Free Legal Advice
events.description: A law student at the shelter knows things. She speaks fast and uses words you might not know.
events.narrator_line: Pro bono is Latin for 'someone else paid for this education.'

events.title: The Shift Change Delay
events.description: New shift is late. The current agents want to leave. Processing speed doubles.
events.narrator_line: The desire to clock out is more powerful than federal training.

events.title: The Document Maker
events.description: Someone in the motel parking lot can make things look more official. For a fee.
events.narrator_line: The line between forgery and graphic design is drawn by intent.

events.title: The Wall Graffiti
events.description: Someone scratched phone numbers into the bathroom wall. One of them is local.
events.narrator_line: The most important information in America is written on bathroom walls.

events.title: The Dropped Badge
events.description: An agent's ID badge is on the ground near the break area. It has a first name and a photo.
events.narrator_line: A badge is a face with clearance. Without the lanyard, it's just a face.

events.title: The Bulletin Board
events.description: A community board at the shelter has bus routes, shelter addresses, and a drawing of a hot dog.
events.narrator_line: Survival information and children's art share wall space democratically.

events.title: The Overheard Radio
events.description: An agent's radio crackles with shift assignments. You catch a frequency and a name.
events.narrator_line: Eavesdropping on government communications is illegal. Overhearing them is just being present.

events.title: The Previous Occupant's Note
events.description: Under the motel mattress: a note in Spanish. Routes. Names. A date from three weeks ago.
events.narrator_line: The motel room's previous guest left a review. It was not on Yelp.

events.title: The Newspaper Clipping
events.description: A folded newspaper page about the hot dog eating contest. Registration details. Entry requirements. A phone number.
events.narrator_line: Competitive eating is covered in the sports section. This tells you everything about America.

events.title: The Map on the Napkin
events.description: Someone drew a rough map of the area on a napkin. X marks something. It might be a rest stop.
events.narrator_line: Cartography has really relaxed its standards.

events.title: The Schedule Posted Wrong
events.description: A shift schedule is visible through the break room window. It was supposed to face the other way.
events.narrator_line: Information security is only as strong as the person who hung the schedule.

events.title: Dawn at the Crossing
events.description: The sun rises on both sides of the border at the same time. This seems worth mentioning.
events.narrator_line: The sun does not recognize sovereignty. Nor, technically, does the wind.

events.title: The Waiting Room
events.description: Plastic chairs. A water fountain that doesn't work. A poster about your rights in seven languages.
events.narrator_line: Your rights are laminated. This should not be comforting but somehow is.

events.title: Sunset on the Highway
events.description: The road stretches north. The sky is doing that thing where it's every color.
events.narrator_line: The highway does not end. It changes its name.

events.title: The Sound of Helicopters
events.description: A helicopter passes overhead. It is probably not about you. Probably.
events.narrator_line: Helicopters are the government's way of making sure you look up.

events.title: The Quiet Hour
events.description: Between 3 and 4 AM, even the border is quiet. You can hear the desert.
events.narrator_line: The desert sounds like nothing. Which is to say, it sounds like possibility.

events.title: A Child's Drawing
events.description: Taped to the shelter wall: a crayon drawing of a house with a red door. The family is stick figures. Everyone is smiling.
events.narrator_line: The red door is the only thing with a specific color. This is a deliberate artistic choice.

events.title: The Flag Lowering
events.description: Two agents lower the flag at sunset. They fold it with the precision of people who were taught this once and never forgot.
events.narrator_line: The ceremony is the same whether anyone watches or not. This is either admirable or compulsive.

locations.name: Transit Hub
locations.description: Everything here is between somewhere and somewhere else. Including you. Including the sandwich in the vending machine.
ambient_details: The departure board flickers between DELAYED and a font that doesn't exist.
A woman sleeps across three seats with the confidence of someone who has done this before.
The vending machine has a handwritten sign: OUT OF ORDER (EXCEPT C4 AND D7).
The announcer pronounces every city name wrong. This appears to be intentional.
Someone left a Bible on the bench. It is bookmarked at Exodus.
The bathroom costs fifty cents. This is somehow the most honest transaction available.
A man in a suit sleeps with his briefcase chained to his wrist. The briefcase has a sticker from Cancun.
The TV is set to a channel that only shows local car dealership ads. It has been this way for years.
The floor is recently mopped. The janitor looks at you the way people look at wet floors.
A payphone still works. This feels like a miracle or a trap.

events.title: The Ticket Counter
events.description: The clerk types slowly. Every keystroke is a judgment.
events.narrator_line: A bus ticket is a receipt for distance.

events.title: The Overnight Conductor
events.description: He checks tickets by flashlight. His handwriting on the tag above your seat is illegible.
events.narrator_line: The conductor has seen 40,000 faces. He remembers the ones who fidget.

events.title: The Chatty Seatmate
events.description: She wants to know where you're going. And where you're from. And why.
events.narrator_line: American friendliness is indistinguishable from interrogation, except for the snacks.

events.title: The Rideshare Driver
events.description: Four stars. Three air fresheners. One opinion about everything.
events.narrator_line: The gig economy turned every car into a confessional with a rating system.

events.title: The Rest Stop Janitor
events.description: He mops around you. Not past you, not away from you. Around.
events.narrator_line: The janitor has mapped every face that passes through. He remembers by shoes.

events.title: The TSA Agent
events.description: She asks you to remove your belt, your shoes, and your sense of dignity.
events.narrator_line: Airport security is theater. The audience is also the cast.

events.title: The Café Car Attendant
events.description: Microwaved burrito. Three dollars. He has opinions about trains that he will share.
events.narrator_line: The café car is the train's living room. The burrito is the train's personality.

events.title: The Trucker at the Rest Stop
events.description: He leans on his cab and offers you a cigarette. The offer includes a destination.
events.narrator_line: Long-haul truckers measure friendship in miles, not years.

events.title: The Station Security Guard
events.description: He walks slow. Watches fast. His flashlight beam finds you like it was looking.
events.narrator_line: Security guards are paid to notice. Some of them do it for free.

events.title: The Vending Machine Repairman
events.description: He has the key to every machine in the station. He is the most powerful person here.
events.narrator_line: Access is power. The vending machine repairman has more keys than the mayor.

events.title: The Overnight Waitress
events.description: Coffee is $1.50 and comes with a lifetime of refills and a look that says 'I've seen worse.'
events.narrator_line: The 24-hour truck stop is America's living room between 2 and 5 AM.

events.title: The Other Passenger
events.description: They're going to the same place. They have a different reason. They want to compare.
events.narrator_line: Shared destinations do not imply shared journeys. Geography has no opinions.

events.title: The Pawn Shop Detour
events.description: Near the station: a pawn shop with a neon OPEN sign and a dust-covered optimism.
events.narrator_line: Pawn shops are where objects go to be honest about their value.

events.title: The Motel Clerk
events.description: The rate is posted. The rate is negotiable. The rate depends on how tired you look.
events.narrator_line: Motel pricing is the free market's most honest expression.

events.title: The Taxi Dispatcher
events.description: She knows every address in the city. She looks at yours and pauses.
events.narrator_line: A pause from a taxi dispatcher is worth a thousand words. Most of them are warnings.

events.title: Bus Breakdown
events.description: The bus makes a sound it shouldn't. Everyone gets off. The next bus is in six hours.
events.narrator_line: Mechanical failure is democracy. Everyone waits equally.

events.title: Random Check
events.description: Border patrol boards the bus at an interior checkpoint. Papers, please.
events.narrator_line: The checkpoint is 100 miles from the border. The Constitution has a flexible definition of 'border.'

events.title: Missed Connection
events.description: The connecting bus left four minutes ago. The next one is tomorrow.
events.narrator_line: Four minutes is either nothing or everything. Right now it is everything.

events.title: Stolen Bag
events.description: Your bag is gone. Your money is in your pocket but everything else is in the bag.
events.narrator_line: The contents of a bag are just objects. The contents of your pockets are your actual priorities.

events.title: Station Closure
events.description: The station closes at midnight. You are inside. Security is not.
events.narrator_line: Being locked inside something is different from being locked out. Both are problems.

events.title: Wrong Ticket
events.description: The ticket says Memphis. You said Dallas. The clerk is gone.
events.narrator_line: The difference between Memphis and Dallas is 451 miles and one clerk's hearing.

events.title: Food Poisoning
events.description: The gas station sushi was a mistake. You knew it then. You know it now.
events.narrator_line: Gas station sushi is not food. It is a dare that comes in a plastic container.

events.title: The Detour
events.description: Road construction adds two hours. The driver seems happy about this.
events.narrator_line: American infrastructure: always improving, never improved.
escape_options: get off and find alternate transport

events.title: Language Barrier
events.description: The automated kiosk is in English only. The help button connects to a recording.
events.narrator_line: The recording thanks you for your patience. It does not speak your language either.

events.title: Suspicious Delay
events.description: The bus waits longer than normal at the stop. No explanation. Someone in a uniform walks through.
events.narrator_line: Unexplained delays are the government's way of taking attendance.

events.title: The Cancelled Ticket
events.description: Someone's cancelled ticket is still valid. The clerk hasn't voided it yet.
events.narrator_line: Waste is someone else's opportunity. This is called economics.

events.title: Day Labor at the Stop
events.description: The rest stop manager needs someone to unload a delivery. Two hours. $40.
events.narrator_line: Physical labor at a rest stop pays more per hour than most philosophy degrees.

events.title: The Free Ride
events.description: A church van is heading the same direction. They have room and sandwiches.
events.narrator_line: The Lord works in mysterious ways. The church van takes I-40.

events.title: Information from a Local
events.description: A regular at the truck stop knows which routes have checkpoints. This week.
events.narrator_line: Local knowledge is worth more than GPS. GPS doesn't know about the new checkpoint.

events.title: The Charging Station
events.description: A diner has outlets and doesn't check if you're a customer.
events.narrator_line: Electricity is the cheapest kindness a business can offer.

events.title: The Return Ticket Buyer
events.description: Someone at the station wants to sell their return ticket. Half price.
events.narrator_line: The secondary ticket market is America's most democratic economy.

events.title: The Trucker's CB
events.description: A trucker lets you listen to the CB radio. Checkpoint locations, road conditions, weather.
events.narrator_line: CB radio: the internet before the internet. Same content. Worse bandwidth.

events.title: The Sleeper Bus
events.description: An overnight bus has a no-show. Empty seat, no ticket needed until the next stop.
events.narrator_line: Empty seats on overnight buses are temporary. Everything on an overnight bus is temporary.

events.title: Translation Help
events.description: Someone speaks your language and English. They offer to help at the counter.
events.narrator_line: Bilingualism is a superpower that pays minimum wage.

events.title: The WiFi Password
events.description: The motel WiFi password is written on the ceiling of the laundry room. You can now look things up.
events.narrator_line: Internet access: the modern equivalent of finding water in the desert.

events.title: Bus Schedule Notes
events.description: Someone annotated a bus schedule with real arrival times. They're all wrong by the same amount.
events.narrator_line: The official schedule is aspirational. The annotations are empirical.

events.title: The Driver's Log
events.description: A driver left his logbook on the seat. Routes, stops, and a note about a checkpoint that moves.
events.narrator_line: The logbook is the driver's diary. The entries are not sentimental.

events.title: The Restroom Message
events.description: Written in marker above the paper towel dispenser: a phone number and the words 'safe house.'
events.narrator_line: Restroom walls are the original social network. The algorithm is gravity.

events.title: The Forgotten Phone
events.description: A phone left in the seat pocket. It's unlocked. The browser has a map open.
events.narrator_line: Someone's digital footprint is now your analog advantage.

events.title: The Station Map
events.description: A transit map with hand-drawn additions. New stops. Unofficial ones.
events.narrator_line: The best maps include places that aren't on any map.

events.title: The Overheard Call
events.description: Someone on the phone mentions your destination city. And a contact. And a price.
events.narrator_line: Eavesdropping is rude. On a bus, it is also unavoidable.

events.title: The Abandoned Backpack
events.description: Under a bench: a backpack with a map, a compass, and three granola bars.
events.narrator_line: The backpack's owner either arrived or didn't. Both explanations are unsettling.

events.title: The Flyer
events.description: A flyer for a job fair in the next city. Some positions don't ask for papers. This is implied, not stated.
events.narrator_line: Job fairs are cattle calls with better lighting. The implied positions have the best pay.

events.title: Highway at Night
events.description: The highway lights pass overhead like a metronome. Inside the bus, everyone is a silhouette.
events.narrator_line: At night on a highway, everyone is going somewhere important. The bus makes no such distinction.

events.title: The 4 AM Stop
events.description: The bus stops in a town whose name you can't read. Five people get off. Nobody gets on.
events.narrator_line: Towns at 4 AM exist only as lights and the sound of a bus door.

events.title: Dawn Through the Window
events.description: The sun comes up on a landscape you've never seen before. It looks like a different planet that grows corn.
events.narrator_line: America is mostly corn and silence, viewed from the correct angle.

events.title: The Engine Sound
events.description: The bus hums at a frequency that could be a lullaby or a warning. You choose lullaby.
events.narrator_line: Engines don't lie. If the sound changes, the situation has changed.

events.title: Rest Stop Sunrise
events.description: The parking lot is empty except for three trucks and the smell of diesel and breakfast.
events.narrator_line: Rest stops at dawn are America's most democratic space. Everyone needs gas.

events.title: The Billboard Parade
events.description: INJURY LAWYER. ADULT STORE. JESUS SAVES. They appear in that order every 30 miles.
events.narrator_line: American billboards tell you everything about the country in three signs.

events.title: Rain on the Bus
events.description: It rains. The bus windows fog. Someone draws a heart. Someone else draws a question mark.
events.narrator_line: Condensation art is the most temporary form of expression. This makes it honest.

locations.name: Mid-America City
locations.description: A place where people know each other's trucks. The Walmart parking lot is the town square. The diner has been serving the same coffee since Vietnam.
ambient_details: The church marquee says GOD KNOWS WHAT YOU DID LAST SUMMER. It has not been updated since July.
A pickup truck idles in the Walmart lot with a bumper sticker that says COEXIST in ammo fonts.
The diner menu has a section called AMERICAN CLASSICS. It is the entire menu.
A teenager skateboarding in the Dollar General parking lot is the most dangerous person in town.
The town has two stoplights. Both are broken. Everyone knows when to stop anyway.
The community bulletin board has a missing cat poster from 2019. The cat's name is Senator.
The gas station has a sign: WE CARD EVERYONE. Below it, in Sharpie: SORRY PASTOR MIKE.
A lawn sprinkler waters a lawn and also the sidewalk and also your shoes.
The local newspaper is four pages. Two of them are coupons.
The high school football field has better lighting than the emergency room.

events.title: The Walmart Greeter
events.description: She says welcome. She means it. She also means she's counting who comes in.
events.narrator_line: Walmart greeters are America's census workers. They just don't file reports.

events.title: The Diner Owner
events.description: He has opinions about the government, the weather, and your order. In that order.
events.narrator_line: Diner owners are the last philosophers. Their medium is pie.

events.title: The County Clerk
events.description: She processes paperwork like it matters. Because it does. To her.
events.narrator_line: County clerks are the immune system of bureaucracy. They reject what doesn't belong.

events.title: The Day Labor Coordinator
events.description: He stands outside Home Depot at 6 AM with a clipboard and a van. His clipboard decides your day.
events.narrator_line: The Home Depot parking lot at dawn is Wall Street for people who actually build things.

events.title: The Laundromat Owner
events.description: She watches soap operas in Spanish while folding strangers' clothes. She knows everything.
events.narrator_line: Laundromats hear every conversation. The machines keep the secrets. The owner does not.

events.title: The Church Secretary
events.description: She does ask questions. She writes the answers in a notebook that isn't for church.
events.narrator_line: Church secretaries know more about the congregation than God does. They take better notes.

events.title: The Small-Town Cop
events.description: Traffic stop. He drives a Crown Vic older than most of his arrests.
events.narrator_line: Small-town cops know every car in town. Yours is not one of them.

events.title: The Farmhand Supervisor
events.description: He needs bodies in the field. He pays in cash and silence. The work starts at dawn.
events.narrator_line: Agriculture runs on two things: sunshine and people whose names are not on any form.

events.title: The Meatpacking Plant Manager
events.description: The plant is hiring. The turnover rate explains why.
events.narrator_line: Meatpacking plants have the highest turnover and the lowest expectations. Both are features.

events.title: The Bodega Owner
events.description: He's from somewhere else too. The store is named after a town he hasn't been back to.
events.narrator_line: Every bodega is named after a place its owner left. This is called branding.

events.title: The Car Wash Owner
events.description: Cash business. He doesn't ask your name. He asks if you can hold a hose.
events.narrator_line: Car washes are the only business where 'under the table' is also a job description.

events.title: The Apartment Super
events.description: He has a unit. No lease. No background check. Cash weekly. The radiator makes a sound.
events.narrator_line: The apartment has character. The character is mostly mold.

events.title: The Temp Agency Receptionist
events.description: She has three positions open. Two require documentation. The third requires 'flexibility.'
events.narrator_line: Temp agencies are the dating apps of employment. Everyone is looking. Nobody reads the fine print.

events.title: The Motel Owner
events.description: She rents by the week. The rate goes down if you stay a month. The room goes up in quality by exactly zero.
events.narrator_line: Weekly rates are the motel's way of saying 'we've given up pretending you're on vacation.'

events.title: The Pawn Shop Dealer
events.description: He doesn't ask questions. He makes offers. The offers are low. The silence is expensive.
events.narrator_line: Pawn shops price things by desperation. The more you need the money, the less everything is worth.

events.title: The ICE Raid
events.description: Unmarked vans at the plant. Everyone runs. Running is suspicious. Not running is suspicious.
events.narrator_line: In an ICE raid, the optimal strategy is to not be there. This is also the optimal strategy for the workplace.

events.title: Small Town Gossip
events.description: The new face in town is news. You are the news. The diner discusses you between bites.
events.narrator_line: In a town of 2,000, privacy is a population of one.

events.title: No Cash Left
events.description: Your money is gone. The next job doesn't pay until Friday.
events.narrator_line: Poverty is a math problem with no variables you control.

events.title: The Workplace Injury
events.description: You can't go to a hospital. The cut is deep enough to need one.
events.narrator_line: Healthcare access is the question. The answer depends on your paperwork.

events.title: The Landlord Problem
events.description: The super wants more money. Or he tells someone. This was not in the original arrangement.
events.narrator_line: Informal arrangements are revised informally. The new terms favor the person with the keys.

events.title: Suspicious Neighbor
events.description: The neighbor watches you leave. Watches you return. Writes down your car's license plate. You don't have a car.
events.narrator_line: Vigilance in suburbia is indistinguishable from boredom with a notebook.

events.title: The Traffic Stop
events.description: Pulled over while getting a ride. The driver's registration is expired. Now it's everyone's problem.
events.narrator_line: Traffic stops are where individual problems become collective ones.

events.title: Weather Delay
events.description: Tornado warning. Everything closes. The sky turns green.
events.narrator_line: Tornadoes do not check immigration status. This is one of their few redeeming qualities.

events.title: The Scam
events.description: The room you paid for doesn't exist. The man who took your money does, but he's gone.
events.narrator_line: Scams targeting undocumented people are unreportable crimes. This is the business model.

events.title: The Flat Tire (Again)
events.description: The ride to the bus station breaks down. It's five miles. It's raining.
events.narrator_line: Walking in rain is either romantic or desperate. You are not in a movie.

events.title: The Church Fund
events.description: The pastor has an emergency fund. No ID required. Just a conversation.
events.narrator_line: Emergency funds are measured in compassion. The interest rate is zero.

events.title: The Restaurant Kitchen
events.description: The kitchen needs a dishwasher. Tonight. Cash at the end of shift.
events.narrator_line: Dishwashing is the entry-level position of every immigrant story ever told.

events.title: The Yard Sale Find
events.description: A yard sale has a working phone for $15. The previous owner cleared their search history.
events.narrator_line: Yard sales are archaeology for the recently discarded.

events.title: The Community Garden
events.description: A community garden has more vegetables than gardeners. They share.
events.narrator_line: Community gardens are communism that works. Nobody tells the gardeners.

events.title: The Library Card
events.description: The library doesn't check residency for a guest pass. Internet, AC, and silence.
events.narrator_line: Libraries are the only public space in America where you can exist for free without buying something.

events.title: The Construction Gig
events.description: A contractor needs help for a week. $500. He doesn't ask for papers. He asks if you're afraid of heights.
events.narrator_line: Construction: where fear of heights pays less than pretending you're not afraid.

events.title: The Goodwill Run
events.description: Goodwill has winter coats for $3 and shoes for $5. The fitting room doesn't require a membership.
events.narrator_line: Goodwill: where someone else's discard becomes your infrastructure.

events.title: The Carpool
events.description: Workers at the plant carpool east. They have room. They're going through Ohio.
events.narrator_line: Carpooling is trust measured in gasoline.

events.title: The Translator Job
events.description: A clinic needs a translator for two hours. They pay $20/hour. Your language skill matters.
events.narrator_line: Being bilingual is a minimum-wage superpower. Unless you're in a clinic that needs you.

events.title: The Friendly Farmer
events.description: A farmer has a room above the barn. Work mornings, travel afternoons. A fair trade.
events.narrator_line: Barns smell like hay and honest labor. Hotels smell like air freshener and credit card fees.

events.title: The Bulletin Board
events.description: The laundromat bulletin board has job listings, bus schedules, and a flyer in Spanish that says 'Don't talk to ICE.'
events.narrator_line: Community information networks predate the internet. They also have better moderation.

events.title: The Hidden Shrine
events.description: Behind the dollar store: a small shrine with candles, a photo, and a note. Someone was here before you.
events.narrator_line: Shrines mark the places where someone needed more than what was available.

events.title: The Overheard Confession
events.description: At the diner: two men talk about a route east that avoids the interstate. One draws on a napkin.
events.narrator_line: The best routes are drawn on napkins by people who have walked them.

events.title: The Library Computer
events.description: The library computer has someone's bookmarks still open. Bus routes. Shelter addresses. A map of New York.
events.narrator_line: Browser history is autobiography. Someone else's browser history is espionage.

events.title: The News Report
events.description: The TV at the diner shows a news segment about the hot dog contest. Registration closes July 3rd.
events.narrator_line: Competitive eating makes the news cycle. Immigration does not. Priorities are clear.

events.title: The Worker's Map
events.description: A coworker at the plant has a hand-drawn map of routes to New York. She offers to copy it.
events.narrator_line: Maps drawn by hand carry the weight of experience. GPS carries the weight of satellites.

events.title: The Phone Number
events.description: Written inside a Bible at the church: a New York phone number and the name 'Miguel.'
events.narrator_line: The Bible contains many messages. This one has a 718 area code.

events.title: The Pamphlet
events.description: A legal aid pamphlet in the clinic waiting room. Know Your Rights. In twelve languages.
events.narrator_line: Rights are more portable than you think. The pamphlet fits in a pocket.

events.title: Main Street at Noon
events.description: The street is empty. The sun is direct. A flag hangs limp on the courthouse.
events.narrator_line: Main Street at noon: everyone is inside. The heat has opinions about outdoor activity.

events.title: Friday Night Lights
events.description: The high school football game lights up the sky. Half the town is there. You are not invited but nobody checks.
events.narrator_line: Football games are the town's heartbeat. The concession stand is its digestive system.

events.title: Sunday Morning
events.description: Church bells. Empty streets. The Walmart parking lot is, for once, not full.
events.narrator_line: Sunday morning is the only time America rests. It lasts approximately three hours.

events.title: The Harvest Moon
events.description: The moon is full over the cornfields. The corn is taller than you.
events.narrator_line: Corn at night is an aesthetic experience that horror movies have ruined for everyone.

events.title: The Storm Front
events.description: The sky goes dark at 2 PM. Lightning strikes in a field. The diner doesn't close.
events.narrator_line: Midwestern storms are dramatic but professional. They arrive, perform, and leave.

events.title: The Train at Night
events.description: A freight train passes through at 1 AM. It takes four minutes. The motel shakes.
events.narrator_line: Freight trains carry America's commerce and insomnia in equal measure.

events.title: The Empty Lot
events.description: An empty lot between two buildings. Someone left a shopping cart and a rain-damaged couch. It is the town's accidental park.
events.narrator_line: Empty lots are nature's way of reclaiming real estate. The couch is nature's way of saying 'sit down.'

locations.name: NYC Outer Borough
locations.description: Seven million people who have all agreed to ignore each other. The subway smells like ambition and urine. Rent is a competitive sport.
ambient_details: A bodega cat sits on the ATM. It has been doing this since the Bloomberg administration.
The subway doors open. No one gets off. Everyone gets on. This is physically impossible but happens daily.
A fruit stand sells mangoes, plantains, and phone chargers. This makes perfect sense.
Someone is playing saxophone in the station. They are better than they should be. This is suspicious.
The 7 train arrives. It is both late and somehow earlier than expected.
A restaurant menu is in four languages. The prices are in a fifth: whatever they feel like today.
The check cashing place has bulletproof glass and a bowl of free candy. The duality of commerce.
A man sells umbrellas that appear only when it rains and vanish when it doesn't.
The fire escape has a chair, an ashtray, and a view of the entire neighborhood. It is someone's office.
A pigeon walks into the bodega. The owner addresses it by name.

events.title: The Bodega Transaction
events.description: The owner knows you don't live here. He sells you the coffee anyway. The cat watches.
events.narrator_line: Bodega cats are the true gatekeepers of New York. They have tenure.

events.title: The Subway Booth Clerk
events.description: She slides the MetroCard under the glass. She's seen your face before. Or one like it.
events.narrator_line: Subway booth clerks exist in a dimension between help desk and oracle.

events.title: The Check Cashing Teller
events.description: Behind bulletproof glass, she processes your money with the efficiency of someone who has processed everyone's money.
events.narrator_line: Check cashing places charge 2% for the privilege of accessing your own money. This is called financial services.

events.title: The Flophouse Manager
events.description: Third floor. Shared bathroom. No guests after 10. The rules are on the wall. The exceptions are negotiable.
events.narrator_line: SROs are New York's affordable housing. The definition of 'affordable' is flexible.

events.title: The Food Cart Vendor
events.description: Lamb over rice. He asks where you're from. He's from somewhere near where you're from.
events.narrator_line: Food carts are embassies with hot sauce.

events.title: The Gypsy Cab Driver
events.description: No meter. A price is named. The price is final. The route is scenic.
events.narrator_line: Gypsy cabs run on trust and cash. The meter is the driver's face.

events.title: The Kitchen Manager
events.description: He needs prep cooks. English not required. Knife skills preferred. The pay is daily.
events.narrator_line: Restaurant kitchens are the most integrated workplaces in America. Nobody notices because they're too busy cooking.

events.title: The Day Labor Corner
events.description: Red Hook. 6 AM. Trucks pull up. Hands go up. If you're picked, you work. If you're not, you wait.
events.narrator_line: Day labor corners are job fairs without the pretense. The resume is your presence.

events.title: The Street Vendor
events.description: Phone cases, chargers, and sunglasses. He sets up at 7 AM and leaves when the cops come.
events.narrator_line: Street vendors are entrepreneurs who file their taxes with their feet.

events.title: The Barbershop Conversation
events.description: The barber knows everyone. A haircut costs $10. The information is free.
events.narrator_line: Barbershops are intelligence agencies with better chairs.

events.title: The Social Worker
events.description: She has a stack of files and a look that says 'I want to help but the system doesn't.'
events.narrator_line: Social workers carry the weight of every case they've ever opened. The closed ones are heavier.

events.title: The Building Super
events.description: He has a basement room. It's not legal. He knows this. You know this. The handshake is the lease.
events.narrator_line: Basement apartments are New York's open secret. The ceiling is someone else's floor.

events.title: The Pawnbroker
events.description: Fordham Road. Gold chains and guitars in the window. He appraises you before he appraises anything else.
events.narrator_line: Pawnbrokers are therapists for objects. They help things find new owners.

events.title: The Fish Market Worker
events.description: Fulton. 3 AM. He's been here since midnight. He offers you coffee and a look at the Statue of Liberty across the water.
events.narrator_line: The fish market at Fulton has the best view of liberty. It smells like commerce.

events.title: The Laundromat Connection
events.description: Sunset Park. She speaks Mandarin, Spanish, and enough English. She has a cousin who has a friend.
events.narrator_line: Immigrant networks are LinkedIn without the performative congratulations.

events.title: NYPD Stop and Chat
events.description: Two officers. They're not stopping you. They're 'asking questions.' The distinction is legal, not practical.
events.narrator_line: A stop is a stop. A chat is voluntary. The difference requires a law degree to identify.

events.title: The Wrong Train
events.description: You're on the F. You needed the 7. You are now in a neighborhood you cannot pronounce.
events.narrator_line: The subway map is a lie agreed upon by millions. The truth is found at your stop.

events.title: Rent Due
events.description: The super wants this week's money. Today. Not tomorrow.
events.narrator_line: In New York, rent is due the day before you have it.

events.title: The Scam Artist
events.description: Three-card monte on the sidewalk. You know it's a scam. Your $20 doesn't.
events.narrator_line: Three-card monte is a lesson in probability that costs exactly what you can't afford.

events.title: Subway Service Change
events.description: Weekend service changes. The 7 doesn't go to Coney Island. Nothing goes to Coney Island. Except the bus.
events.narrator_line: MTA weekend service is the transit authority's way of saying 'we're working on it' since 1953.

events.title: The Language Wall
events.description: The form is in English. The instructions are in English. The person who can help speaks only English.
events.narrator_line: Monolingualism is a feature of empire, not a bug.

events.title: The Closed Shelter
events.description: The shelter is full. Has been since Tuesday. The waitlist is a phone number.
events.narrator_line: Full shelters are New York's most consistent product.

events.title: Heat Wave
events.description: 98 degrees. The subway is 110. The sidewalk is 140. The fire hydrant is open but the cops are watching.
events.narrator_line: New York in summer is a city-wide sauna. The dress code is survival.

events.title: The Missing Contact
events.description: The person you were supposed to meet isn't here. The address is right. They're just gone.
events.narrator_line: People disappear in New York all the time. Most of them are just in another borough.

events.title: The Expired MetroCard
events.description: The turnstile says no. The booth clerk says no. Your options say no. The fare is $2.90.
events.narrator_line: $2.90 is either pocket change or a crisis. Context is everything.

events.title: The Community Fridge
events.description: A community fridge on a corner in Bushwick. Free food. No questions. A sign says 'Take what you need.'
events.narrator_line: Community fridges are mutual aid in appliance form.

events.title: The Under-the-Table Gig
events.description: A restaurant needs someone for tonight's shift. Cash. 6 hours. Walk-in interview = showing up.
events.narrator_line: Walk-in interviews in New York: you walked in. You're hired. Now run the dishwasher.

events.title: The Subway Musician's Tip
events.description: The saxophone player knows a place in Flatbush. Cheap. Safe. He writes the address on a napkin.
events.narrator_line: Subway musicians are the city's nervous system. They feel everything.

events.title: The Cousin's Cousin
events.description: Someone in the bodega knows someone who knows someone who needs a worker. The chain of someones leads somewhere.
events.narrator_line: Immigrant networks have a 100% connection rate. LinkedIn wishes.

events.title: Free Clinic Day
events.description: A clinic in Jackson Heights does free checkups on Thursdays. Today is Thursday.
events.narrator_line: Free clinic day: the only day the medical system works exactly as it should.

events.title: The Contest Flyer
events.description: A flyer for the Nathan's hot dog eating contest. Registration. Rules. A map of Coney Island.
events.narrator_line: The flyer promises fame, glory, and unlimited hot dogs. Two of these are true.

events.title: The Park Bench Connection
events.description: An old man on a bench in Flushing Meadows. He's been in New York since 1982. He has advice.
events.narrator_line: Park bench wisdom is America's most undervalued asset class.

events.title: The Moving Job
events.description: Someone in the neighborhood is moving. They need three bodies and a truck. $100 each. Half a day.
events.narrator_line: Moving day in New York is everyone's nightmare and someone else's income.

events.title: The Phone Repair Shop
events.description: A phone repair shop fixes your cracked screen for $20. The owner adds his number. 'In case you need anything.'
events.narrator_line: Phone repair shops are the modern village well. Everyone visits. Everyone talks.

events.title: The Legal Aid Clinic
events.description: Walk-in hours at a legal aid office. A tired lawyer with a good heart and 47 cases.
events.narrator_line: Legal aid lawyers are the last idealists. Their caseloads are their penance.

events.title: The Community Board Notice
events.description: A community board posting about the hot dog contest. Spectator entry is free. Contestant registration requires a form.
events.narrator_line: Bureaucracy follows you even to competitive eating.

events.title: The Kitchen Gossip
events.description: In the restaurant kitchen: someone mentions a contact at Nathan's. They need workers for setup.
events.narrator_line: Restaurant kitchens are where information goes to get seasoned.

events.title: The Subway Map Notes
events.description: Someone annotated a subway map with safe spots, shelters, and the words 'avoid 34th street on Fridays.'
events.narrator_line: Annotated subway maps are urban survival guides disguised as vandalism.

events.title: The Newspaper Stand
events.description: A Spanish-language newspaper has a feature on the contest. It includes a map and a schedule.
events.narrator_line: The contest makes the Spanish papers too. Hot dogs transcend language.

events.title: The Taxi Driver's Advice
events.description: The cab driver has driven to Coney Island 500 times. He knows the back entrance to the contest area.
events.narrator_line: Taxi drivers know every entrance to everything. It's a professional requirement.

events.title: The Flyer Under the Door
events.description: Someone slid a flyer under the flophouse door. Coney Island directions. Bus routes. A hand-drawn hot dog.
events.narrator_line: The hand-drawn hot dog has more artistic merit than the flyer's author intended.

events.title: The Overheard Strategy
events.description: Two men at the bodega discuss competitive eating strategy. One has done research. The other has done practice.
events.narrator_line: Competitive eating preparation is either science or madness. The literature is unclear.

events.title: The Phone Number on the Wall
events.description: A phone number written on the wall of the flophouse bathroom. Below it: 'Coney Island. Ask for Hector.'
events.narrator_line: Hector's reputation precedes him. His phone number follows.

events.title: The 7 Train View
events.description: From the elevated 7 train, Queens unfolds below. A thousand lives in a thousand windows.
events.narrator_line: The 7 train is a horizontal elevator through every country on earth.

events.title: The Bodega at Midnight
events.description: Fluorescent light spills onto the sidewalk. Inside: everything you need and nothing you want.
events.narrator_line: Bodegas at midnight are convenience stores in the existential sense.

events.title: The Rooftop View
events.description: From the roof of the flophouse: the Manhattan skyline. It looks like a promise made in neon.
events.narrator_line: Manhattan from a distance is beautiful. Manhattan from inside is expensive.

events.title: The Playground
events.description: Kids play in a sprinkler. They speak four languages. None of them are English.
events.narrator_line: The playground is the most multilingual institution in America. Nobody filed for a permit.

events.title: The Street at Rush Hour
events.description: Eight million people move. The sidewalk flows like a river with elbows.
events.narrator_line: Rush hour is proof that humans can cooperate. The cooperation looks like ignoring each other.

events.title: The Fire Escape Garden
events.description: Someone grows tomatoes on a fire escape in the Bronx. They're the best tomatoes you've ever seen.
events.narrator_line: Fire escape gardens are agriculture's most vertical expression.

events.title: The Last Stop
events.description: Stillwell Avenue. End of the line. The doors open to salt air and the sound of the ocean.
events.narrator_line: The last stop is where the subway admits it's an island. The ocean has been waiting.

locations.name: Coney Island
locations.description: The end of the subway line. The beginning of the ocean. The hot dog eating contest is in three hours and you can smell the mustard from the boardwalk.
ambient_details: The Cyclone rattles overhead. It has been rattling since 1927. This is either reassuring or terrifying.
A seagull steals a hot dog from a child. The child's father photographs it instead of intervening.
The boardwalk planks creak with the weight of a century of people looking at the same ocean.
Nathan's Famous has a line around the block. The line has its own economy.
A man practices competitive eating on the beach. His technique involves staring at the waves.
The Wonder Wheel turns slowly. From the top you can see the contest stage being assembled.
Someone is spray-painting a portrait of Joey Chestnut on a piece of plywood. It is not commissioned.
The beach has a sign: NO SWIMMING. A man in full clothing walks into the ocean anyway.
A fortune teller's sign says CLOSED FOR LUNCH. The irony is probably intentional.
The smell of mustard is so strong it has become a landmark. Turn left at the mustard.

events.title: The Hot Dog Stand Operator
events.description: Not Nathan's. The other one. He's been here longer and he wants you to know that.
events.narrator_line: In the shadow of Nathan's, every hot dog stand is a statement of defiance.

events.title: The Registration Clerk
events.description: She has a clipboard, a pen, and the power to decide if your paperwork is 'complete enough.'
events.narrator_line: Contest registration is the last bureaucracy between you and competitive eating.

events.title: The Event Coordinator
events.description: He wears a Nathan's Famous polo and the expression of someone managing controlled chaos.
events.narrator_line: Event coordination is just organized panic with a walkie-talkie.

events.title: The Carnival Ride Operator
events.description: He's been running the Tilt-A-Whirl since before you were born. He has stories. And opinions about hot dogs.
events.narrator_line: Carnival ride operators see the world in circles. This is both literal and philosophical.

events.title: The Souvenir Shop Owner
events.description: She sells Coney Island t-shirts to people who will never come back. She knows this. She sells them anyway.
events.narrator_line: Souvenir shops sell the idea that a place can fit in a bag. It cannot. This is the business.

events.title: The Beach Security Guard
events.description: He patrols the boardwalk with the energy of someone who peaked in high school football.
events.narrator_line: Beach security is law enforcement's most casual dress code.

events.title: The Fortune Teller
events.description: Madame Zelda. Or possibly Karen. She sees your future. It involves hot dogs.
events.narrator_line: Fortune telling on Coney Island is the only honest profession. Everyone knows it's fake. Everyone listens.

events.title: The Competitive Eater
events.description: He's training on the beach. His method involves staring at waves and eating bread.
events.narrator_line: Competitive eating training is indistinguishable from a very specific picnic.

events.title: The Nathan's Counter Worker
events.description: She serves 500 hot dogs a day. She does not eat hot dogs. She has opinions about people who do.
events.narrator_line: Working at Nathan's during the contest is like working at the Vatican during Easter. With mustard.

events.title: The Lifeguard
events.description: Off duty. On the boardwalk. He watches the water even when he's not being paid to.
events.narrator_line: Lifeguards off duty are still lifeguards. The ocean doesn't clock out.

events.title: The Boardwalk Portrait Artist
events.description: She can draw your face in ten minutes. She asks where you're from while she draws. The portrait looks like someone who made it.
events.narrator_line: Boardwalk portraits capture something photographs miss. Possibly because they're less accurate.

events.title: The Arcade Manager
events.description: He fixes machines older than most of his customers. He keeps score on everything.
events.narrator_line: Arcade managers are museum curators for machines that eat quarters.

events.title: The Cyclone Operator
events.description: She straps people into a roller coaster built in 1927 and says 'have fun' without irony.
events.narrator_line: The Cyclone has outlasted everything except the ocean and the price of hot dogs.

events.title: The Luna Park Custodian
events.description: He's seen every person who's ever thrown up on the Cyclone. He has a ranking system.
events.narrator_line: Custodians at amusement parks are the only honest historians of human capacity.

events.title: The Food Truck Operator
events.description: Near MCU Park. He sells tacos and information. The tacos are better.
events.narrator_line: Food trucks near stadiums are mobile embassies of flavor in a sea of hot dogs.

events.title: Registration Deadline
events.description: Registration closes in two hours. The line is an hour and forty-five minutes.
events.narrator_line: The math is against you. The math has always been against you.

events.title: The ID Check
events.description: Contest registration requires ID. Your ID situation is... complicated.
events.narrator_line: Identity is philosophical. ID is bureaucratic. They are not the same.

events.title: The Crowd
events.description: 50,000 people. All here for hot dogs. Moving through them requires a strategy.
events.narrator_line: Crowd dynamics follow the same physics as fluids. You are a molecule.

events.title: The Security Perimeter
events.description: The contest area is fenced. Security checks bags. Your bag has a story to tell.
events.narrator_line: Security perimeters are circles of suspicion with a gate.

events.title: The Media Scrum
events.description: Cameras. Microphones. Your face is the last thing that should be on TV right now.
events.narrator_line: Fame and anonymity are both survival strategies. You can only choose one.

events.title: The Heat (Weather)
events.description: July 4th on the boardwalk. 95 degrees. The concrete radiates. The hot dogs radiate. You radiate.
events.narrator_line: Coney Island in July is a convection oven with a view.

events.title: Last Dollar
events.description: You have $4. A hot dog is $4. This is either poetry or poverty.
events.narrator_line: The final dollar is the most powerful unit of currency. It decides everything.

events.title: The Wrong Entrance
events.description: The contestant entrance is on the other side. You're going to have to walk the entire boardwalk.
events.narrator_line: The boardwalk is one mile long. With purpose, it feels like ten.

events.title: The Rival
events.description: Another contestant recognizes something in your face. Not your identity. Your desperation.
events.narrator_line: In competitive eating, desperation is either fuel or a tell. Your opponent is deciding which.

events.title: The Phone Dies (Again)
events.description: Your phone dies at the worst possible moment. The contact's booth number was on the screen.
events.narrator_line: Phone batteries die at the exact moment you need them. This is not conspiracy. This is lithium-ion.

events.title: The Setup Crew
events.description: They're building the contest stage. They need one more pair of hands. The pay is access.
events.narrator_line: Access is the most valuable currency at any event. It costs exactly one favor.

events.title: The Press Pass
events.description: A journalist drops their press pass. It has a photo. The photo could be anyone.
events.narrator_line: Press passes are the skeleton keys of public events. The photo is a suggestion.

events.title: The Nathan's Employee
events.description: A Nathan's employee needs a break. You could cover for fifteen minutes. Behind the counter is backstage.
events.narrator_line: Employee substitution: the oldest infiltration technique in the service industry.

events.title: The Local's Shortcut
events.description: A local shows you the gap in the fence behind Luna Park. Everyone knows about it. Including security.
events.narrator_line: Local knowledge is a shortcut to shortcuts.

events.title: The Practice Round
events.description: There's an informal practice round on the beach. Winners get a spot in the qualifier.
events.narrator_line: Practice rounds are where talent meets desperation. The hot dogs are the same.

events.title: The Sponsor Booth
events.description: A sponsor gives away free merchandise. The shirt says CONTESTANT on the back.
events.narrator_line: Branded merchandise is camouflage that someone else paid for.

events.title: The Announcer's Favor
events.description: The contest announcer needs someone to test the microphone. You volunteer. Everyone sees your face. But in a good way.
events.narrator_line: Visibility can be armor or exposure. The difference is context.

events.title: The Beach Find
events.description: Half-buried in the sand: a wallet. $60 inside. A Coney Island annual pass. No ID.
events.narrator_line: The ocean giveth. The sand conceals. Finders keepers is beach law.

events.title: The Volunteer Position
events.description: The contest needs water carriers. Volunteers get access. And all the water you can drink.
events.narrator_line: Volunteering: working for free in exchange for being exactly where you need to be.

events.title: The Last-Minute Dropout
events.description: A contestant drops out. Food poisoning. From hot dogs. The irony is not lost on anyone.
events.narrator_line: Competitive eating injuries are occupational hazards that sound like jokes.

events.title: The Contest Rules
events.description: A discarded copy of the official rules. Section 4.2.1: 'All contestants must present valid identification.' Section 4.2.2: 'See Section 4.2.1.'
events.narrator_line: The rules are circular. Like most institutional documents.

events.title: The Backstage Map
events.description: A production assistant's map of the backstage area. Entrances, exits, and the location of the mustard.
events.narrator_line: Backstage maps are treasure maps for people who value access over gold.

events.title: The Competitor List
events.description: A printed list of contestants. Your name is not on it. One name is crossed out.
events.narrator_line: Lists are power. Not being on a list is either freedom or exclusion.

events.title: The Vendor Gossip
events.description: A food truck vendor knows which security guard takes long breaks. And when.
events.narrator_line: Vendor networks know more about event security than event security does.

events.title: The Program Notes
events.description: The event program has a schedule. The schedule has gaps. Gaps are opportunities.
events.narrator_line: Event schedules are aspirational documents. The gaps are where reality lives.

events.title: The Discarded Walkie
events.description: A walkie-talkie left on a bench. It still works. Channel 3 is security. Channel 7 is production.
events.narrator_line: A walkie-talkie is a window into the nervous system of any operation.

events.title: The Spray-Painted Map
events.description: On the boardwalk: someone spray-painted directions to the contest in three languages.
events.narrator_line: Graffiti is urban wayfinding for people who don't trust Google Maps.

events.title: The Old-Timer's Story
events.description: A man who's watched every contest since 1972 tells you about the year someone entered without registration.
events.narrator_line: Oral history is more useful than written history. It comes with editorial commentary.

events.title: The Boardwalk at Dawn
events.description: Empty. The ocean is the only thing awake. The contest stage sits empty under bunting that snaps in the wind.
events.narrator_line: Coney Island before the crowds is a stage before the play. The ocean is the orchestra warming up.

events.title: The Smell of Mustard
events.description: It's everywhere. In the air. In your clothes. In the concept of Coney Island itself.
events.narrator_line: Mustard is Coney Island's perfume. You will smell it for weeks after you leave.

events.title: The Fireworks Setup
events.description: Workers wire the fireworks on the beach. July 4th from the detonator's perspective.
events.narrator_line: Fireworks are controlled explosions celebrating the founding of a country through uncontrolled explosions.

events.title: The Ocean
events.description: It's right there. It's been there the whole time. You just couldn't see it until now.
events.narrator_line: The Atlantic Ocean is the finish line for everyone traveling east. It has no opinion about your arrival.

events.title: The Crowd Gathers
events.description: People fill the boardwalk. Families. Tourists. Competitive eating enthusiasts, which is apparently a demographic.
events.narrator_line: 50,000 people gather to watch other people eat hot dogs. Democracy is beautiful.

events.title: The National Anthem
events.description: Someone sings the anthem over a PA system. Everyone stops. You stop too. For different reasons.
events.narrator_line: The national anthem sounds different from the inside than from the outside. You are learning the difference.

events.title: The Countdown
events.description: Three. Two. One. The contest begins. Whether you're in it or watching, this is the end of the road.
events.narrator_line: Every journey ends with a countdown. Yours involved more hot dogs than most.
